added_lines: in today's gospel from matthew jesus faces the first challenge to his teachings from the pharisees. they failed to see jesus as the word of god, the love of god and the power of god. all they saw was someone breaking their laws. they tried to trap jesus into saying something with which they could condemn him. a delegation composed of pharisees who hated rome and some herodians who worked with rome approached jesus with a question. both sides hated each other but their hatred of jesus united them. they open their conversation flattering jesus for his honesty and sense of justice. jesus saw through their hypocrisy at once. they then posed the question : "tell us then, what you think. is it lawful to pay taxes to caesar or not? this question put jesus in a difficult position as the pharisees did not want to pay taxes to the romans while the herodians were willing to pay taxes. jesus knows that the answer to the question is not what the group is interested in rather they want to trap jesus into a yes or no answer which would alienate one or other section of the community against him. jesus asks them to show him a coin. on the coin is the head of caesar. jesus answers their question "give therefore to caesar the things that are caesar's and to god the things that are god's.” in some ways we are people of this world and also of jesus. our loyalties as christians are first to god and then trying to make the world a better place through living as witnesses of god's word. there can be times when there is conflict, we can’t allow our loyalty to earthly goods ever to overcome our loyalty to god. where there's disrespect for life, injustice, war, racism, or any other evils in our society our loyalty to god moves us to speak and work to alleviate such things. we are obliged to be positive and speak the truth in love. since god’s image is stamped on each baptized person he or she is owned by him and so must give himself or herself to him. as st. thomas more said "the king’s good servant, but god's first.

. prayer for vocations! heavenly father, you call each of us by name and invite us to follow your son with generous hearts. pour out your holy spirit upon our diocese of kerry, that young people may encounter christ and have the courage to answer your call. raise up holy priests to proclaim your word, celebrate the eucharist with joy, and serve your people with humble love. strengthen those already called to be faithful witnesses to the gospel. through the prayers of mary, mother of the church, and st brendan, our patron saint, bless our diocese with joyful and generous vocations to the priesthood, for the glory of your name and the life of the world. we ask this through christ our lord . amen. cahersiveen
